claim: Self-organizing traffic signal timing through information-theoretic optimization
mechanism: Each intersection adjusts its signal timing to maximize the information flow through the network, measured by the mutual information between upstream and downstream traffic states. This creates a system where signals adapt to maximize overall network throughput rather than just local efficiency
evidence: Myxomycetes optimize network structures for efficient resource flow
Information theory has been applied to traffic flow analysis
Self-organizing systems often optimize information transfer
assumptions: Maximizing information flow correlates with maximizing traffic throughput
Local measurements can estimate network-wide information flow
Information-theoretic optimization is computationally feasible in real-time
The network has sufficient heterogeneity to benefit from information maximization
expected_failure_modes: Misalignment between information flow and actual traffic efficiency
Sensitivity to measurement errors in traffic state estimation
Failure to handle extreme traffic conditions
novelty_rationale: Applies information-theoretic principles to traffic signal control, framing the problem as maximizing information flow rather than traditional metrics like delay or throughput, potentially revealing new optimization strategies
testability: Can be tested by implementing information-theoretic signal control algorithms and comparing performance to traditional methods across various traffic scenarios
falsifier: If the system fails to improve traffic flow compared to traditional optimization methods, or if the computational complexity prevents real-time operation
